brief.title: Malaria: A Preventable Killer — Global Progress and the Road Ahead
brief.one_liner: Over half a million people still die from malaria each year, most of them children, yet humanity has made remarkable progress eliminating the disease from half the world.
brief.goal: Viewers should understand the scale of malaria's toll on children and vulnerable populations, recognize the dramatic historical progress in eliminating the disease from many regions, and appreciate the interventions — bednets, vaccines, and economic development — that can continue driving progress.

sections.title: The Burden: Who Malaria Kills
sections.objective: Convey the scale of annual deaths, emphasizing that children under 5 are the most vulnerable group and Africa bears the overwhelming majority of the burden.

sections.title: From Half the World to a Quarter
sections.objective: Show that malaria was once endemic across ~50% of the world's land surface and has been eliminated from many regions, shrinking to ~27% by 2002. Emphasize that malaria is not inherently a 'tropical disease' but one that was eliminated everywhere except the tropics.

sections.title: Death Toll Trends: 2000–2023
sections.objective: Present the decline in deaths from 2000 to 2015, the stalling of progress, and the COVID-19 setback in 2020, using WHO and IHME estimates.

sections.title: What Works: Tools to Beat Malaria
sections.objective: Highlight the three key drivers of elimination — insecticide-treated bednets, public health measures/vaccines, and economic development — as actionable levers for continued progress.

sections.title: 1,320 Children Every Day
sections.objective: Leave viewers with the urgency: 1,320 children die from this preventable disease daily, and continued investment can change that.
